principle_text: When the seller discloses key features of the item, you should inquire further to prompt price reductions or additional concessions.
When the seller affirms the good condition of the item without addressing the price difference, avoid solely focusing on product details and not pushing for a lower price.

When the seller acknowledges a low offer and counters with a slightly reduced price, you should make firm but reasonable counteroffers to create downward pressure on the price and improve your leverage.
When the seller highlights positive aspects of the property, avoid not using this information to negotiate for a lower price, as it may undermine your leverage in the bargaining process.
When the seller indicates the buyer's offer is too high, avoid lowering the offer too quickly as it weakens the buyer's leverage in negotiations.

When the seller emphasizes product features and usage history without addressing the price discrepancy, avoid solely focusing on gathering more product information instead of steering the conversation towards negotiating a better deal.
When the seller initiates the conversation with a question, avoid responding with a simple greeting that lacks negotiation content or price discussion.
When the seller discloses that the item was lightly used, avoid accepting the initial price without negotiating for a lower one based on its secondhand status.
When the seller confirms good condition and usage history of the item, avoid focusing solely on product condition and inquire about price adjustments to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller affirms the listing details without altering the price, avoid providing additional information that could potentially weaken your negotiation position.
When the seller offers a price that the buyer finds too high, the buyer should directly ask for negotiation to establish leverage and open the discussion for potential price reduction.
When the seller provides product details without mentioning pricing, avoid making an offer or negotiating on price to prevent revealing your position prematurely.
When the seller immediately accepts the buyer's proposed price and adds extra value, such as free delivery, it strengthens the buyer's position and enhances the deal.
When the seller focuses on product details, avoid failing to address price negotiation to ensure maintaining leverage in securing a lower price.

When the seller describes the item's condition and attributes, avoid failing to link these positive aspects to price negotiation or leverage, as it may miss opportunities to influence the buyer's offer.

When the buyer's utterance is irrelevant to the negotiation topic, avoid engaging in non-related banter and steer the conversation back to the item being discussed to maintain focus on the negotiation.
When the seller sets the initial price and offers a conditional discount, avoid providing a simple affirmation of interest without negotiating the price or terms upfront.
When the seller confirms the item's condition, avoid repeating the same information to create leverage for justifying a lower price.
When the seller confirms the item's age and emphasizes its good condition, avoid making price adjustments or concessions to maintain your negotiation position.
When the seller immediately accepts a reduced price without counteroffering, you should clarify your interest in purchasing only one item to secure a better deal.
When the seller introduces additional costs or justifications for a higher price, avoid delaying price negotiation by not leveraging potential value-adds like included items or needed repairs.

When the seller reiterates the initial price and mentions other interested buyers, avoid expressing enthusiasm without introducing negotiation tactics to create leverage and pressure for a lower price.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by asking for a specific counteroffer, you should propose a lower price to advance the negotiation and establish a starting point for price discussion.
When the buyer asks about stains or marks on the item, avoid delaying responses as it can hinder the negotiation progress and buyer's assessment of the item's value.
When the seller emphasizes the product's value without committing to a price reduction, avoid making emotional appeals without concrete leverage or specific counteroffers.
When the seller states the firm price of $80 each without any concessions, avoid making minimal and vague utterances that fail to establish leverage or negotiation intent.
When the seller emphasizes the low usage of the item, avoid confirming interest without proposing a counteroffer or leveraging this information to negotiate a lower price.

When the seller confirms the item's excellent condition but reveals personal urgency to sell, avoid focusing solely on factual questions and seek to leverage the seller's urgency in negotiating the price.
When the seller states their initial price without acknowledging the buyer's lower starting point, avoid making a simple acknowledgment of interest that does not influence the price negotiation.
When the seller mentions a specific flaw in the item, avoid making generic compliments that do not address pricing or leverage, as it may not lead to progress in negotiating a lower price.

When the seller emphasizes the item's newness and condition, avoid asking questions that do not directly address price negotiation to prevent reinforcing the seller's position on the initial asking price.
When the seller emphasizes product quality and additional services without mentioning price concessions, avoid making non-price-related inquiries that do not advance your negotiation leverage.
When the buyer expresses interest without mentioning price or terms, avoid responding with generic questions that do not advance the negotiation toward pricing or concessions.
When the seller responds with product features and invites questions without addressing price, avoid giving minimal or non-committal replies that do not advance the negotiation.
When the seller clearly states their asking price without concessions, avoid vague expressions of interest that do not initiate price negotiation or establish leverage.
When the seller confirms the item is in good condition without conceding defects, avoid focusing on minor product details that do not directly influence price negotiation.
When the seller indicates openness to negotiation and offers a first price reduction, you should initiate price discussions early to create leverage and encourage further concessions.
When the seller states a firm initial price but shows willingness to negotiate, you should directly ask for a lower price to prompt a favorable concession.
When the seller emphasizes the item's good condition and limited use, avoid making vague or non-specific inquiries that do not directly advance your negotiation position.
When the seller has only greeted and asked about interest without mentioning price, avoid making solely complimentary or neutral statements that do not initiate price negotiation.
When the seller introduces additional costs like delivery fees without changing the item price, avoid ignoring these extra expenses as they affect the total negotiation value.
When the seller emphasizes the item's perfect condition to justify a firm price, avoid asking questions that confirm this condition without challenging the price or negotiating flexibility.
When the seller acknowledges the item's sentimental value and personal circumstances without discussing price, avoid making only positive comments that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller provides detailed information about the item's condition without a price concession, avoid making purely informational inquiries without following up with a price negotiation tactic.
When the seller rejects a low offer and raises their counteroffer, avoid increasing your offer slightly as it may weaken your leverage and encourage the seller to demand a higher price.
When the seller firmly rejects a low offer and emphasizes the item's sentimental value, avoid making an initial offer significantly below your stated budget without justification.
When the seller firmly defends the item's condition and price, avoid making concessions or offering benefits without securing a corresponding price reduction.
When the buyer expresses interest but signals the price is too high, you should invite them to make an offer to encourage active price negotiation and reveal their target price.
When the seller provides detailed product information without addressing price, avoid making neutral inquiries that do not advance price negotiation or create leverage.
When the seller has only initiated contact without discussing price, avoid responding with mere confirmation that does not introduce negotiation or leverage-building tactics.
When the seller responds openly to buyer inquiries without addressing price, avoid immediately pushing for a lower price before gathering more product information.
When the seller confirms the item is in perfect condition without defects, avoid relying solely on condition inquiries to justify a lower price without introducing other negotiation tactics.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition in response to inquiries, avoid asking questions that allow the seller to reinforce the item's high value without addressing price.
When the seller firmly states a non-negotiable price with justification, avoid making an immediate lowball offer that concedes too much too early and risks weakening your negotiation leverage.
When the seller provides detailed product information without adjusting price, avoid asking only informational questions that do not create leverage for negotiating a better price.
When the seller emphasizes product features to justify price without addressing buyer's price concerns, avoid responding with only factual confirmations that do not advance the negotiation on price.
When the seller affirms the item is in excellent condition without indicating flexibility, avoid pressing immediately for a lower price before gathering more negotiation leverage.
When the seller shows openness to negotiation, you should propose a trade or additional value to effectively lower the price to your target.
When the seller responds with a neutral, polite greeting without engaging on price or terms, avoid using only social pleasantries that do not advance the negotiation.
When the seller states the price and mentions a minor flaw without lowering the price further, avoid only asking informational questions without leveraging the flaw to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item is in perfect condition and shares motivation to sell quickly, avoid only asking about product condition without linking it to price or negotiation leverage.
When the seller confirms the item is in pristine condition with no issues, avoid focusing solely on product flaws to negotiate price reductions.
When the seller responds by shifting focus to logistical details, avoid expressing enthusiasm without introducing price negotiation or leverage.

When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition and added value without addressing price, avoid focusing solely on product inquiries that strengthen the seller's justification for a higher price.
When the seller responds neutrally by inviting questions without discussing price, avoid merely confirming interest without introducing negotiation points or price considerations.
When the seller responds by emphasizing product features without addressing price, avoid making only neutral or non-committal statements that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller responds to a low offer by lowering the price and adding value, you should use aggressive anchoring below your initial target to shift the negotiation in your favor.

When the seller reiterates the full list price and offers additional services without lowering it, avoid expressing unconditional enthusiasm that signals acceptance and reduces your leverage to negotiate price.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's usage duration, avoid making vague or irrelevant inquiries that do not build leverage for price negotiation.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's age and condition, avoid making immediate price demands without first using that information to justify your offer.
When the seller responds by emphasizing the original higher price and asks for your budget, avoid immediately pushing a low offer without first gathering detailed product information.
When the seller has introduced the item and its condition, avoid making neutral or unrelated remarks that do not advance the negotiation or address price or terms.
When the seller offers an alternative to direct information requests without addressing price, avoid shifting focus away from price negotiation prematurely.
When the seller has only initiated contact without mentioning price or terms, avoid responding with neutral or non-committal greetings that do not advance negotiation or establish leverage.
When the seller emphasizes the item's high quality and justifies the initial price, you should raise practical concerns that create leverage for negotiating a price reduction and added value.
When the seller provides factual information about the product without indicating flexibility, avoid focusing solely on non-price details that do not advance the negotiation on terms or price.
When the seller reveals product condition details and offers a conditional discount, you should inquire about item condition to prompt price concessions and advance negotiation progress.
When the seller confirms the item’s condition without addressing price, avoid focusing solely on non-price details that do not advance negotiation leverage.
When the seller highlights excellent product condition and raises the price, avoid asking questions that confirm quality without preparing to counter the increased price demand.
When the seller counters with a price slightly above the buyer's offer, avoid immediately accepting or conceding without further negotiation to maintain leverage.
When the seller provides information about minor flaws without adjusting the price, avoid using purely informational questions without linking them to a price negotiation or concession request.
When the seller confirms the item is clean and lightly used, avoid focusing solely on minor flaws without acknowledging the item's overall good condition.
When the seller counters with a reduced but still firm price, you should use a credible competitor's lower price to justify a further lower offer and create downward pressure on the price.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's condition without indicating price flexibility, avoid relying solely on casual or rapport-building questions to influence the price.
When the seller provides detailed information about the item's excellent condition and recent purchase, avoid making premature price offers without first assessing value and context.
When the seller confirms the item is in great condition without mentioning price, avoid only asking neutral informational questions that do not create leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller acknowledges a defect or damage in the item, you should highlight these flaws to justify a lower price and gain negotiation leverage.
When the seller shares personal positive experiences and product benefits without mentioning price, avoid failing to introduce pricing or negotiation topics to maintain progress in the negotiation.
When the seller justifies a higher price than their initial offer, avoid referencing or anchoring to prices above the seller's stated starting price to prevent strengthening their position.
When the seller confirms the item is in great condition without conceding flaws, avoid focusing solely on condition questions without leveraging that information to negotiate a lower price.
When the seller confirms the item is in great condition and reveals its original high cost, avoid making price offers without first gathering more value-related information.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition and unused, avoid making lowball offers without justification based on product condition.
When the seller reveals the item's condition includes wear or damage, you should ask specific questions about flaws to gain leverage for negotiating a lower price.
